title: SIEM relay contracts with late-arrival compaction and status propagation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Customers integrating Redwood audit streams into external SIEMs (Splunk, Datadog, generic webhook sinks) experience two failure modes: (1) late-arriving events that must be compacted or merged to avoid duplicate alerts/cost blowups, and (2) opaque delivery state so that the originating tenant cannot determine whether a given audit record was accepted, retried, or dropped by the sink. Goal: Define clear relay contracts and implement an adapter pattern that supports compact-on-late-arrival semantics, deterministic idempotency, and explicit status propagation (accepted/retried/failed/dlq) back to tenant dashboards and to the originating audit stream for reconciliation.
acceptance_criteria: Protocol: a compact-enabling relay contract document published (Confluence link) describing sequence identifiers, compaction keys, and compaction windows
Adapters implement idempotency tokens and support a status callback channel used for reconciliation
Late-arrival compaction runs in the relay with configurable window per customer (default 5 minutes) and documented cost/latency tradeoffs
Metrics surfaced: delivery_latency_p50/p95/p99, undelivered_count, compaction_skipped_count, ack_latency
End-to-end test harness reproduces out-of-order + duplicate + transient-failure scenarios with deterministic assertions
No customer reportable data loss for P0 customers beyond configured retention/compaction policy (documented SLA)
Feature flag gate + gradual rollout to 10% tenants then 100% after 2 weeks of telemetry
implementation_notes: Relay contract: each audit record carries (tenant_id, stream_id, sequence_id, compaction_key|null, idempotency_token). sequence_id monotonic per stream; compaction_key groups records that may be compacted (e.g., object update keys)

Late-arrival handling: when a record arrives with sequence_id <= head_of_stream + 1 and compaction_key set, the relay will attempt an in-memory compaction pass before emitting. Compaction is bounded by configured window and by memory budget to avoid amplification.

Status propagation: adapters should optionally post status events back to a Redwood status queue with (original_event_id, external_sink_id, status, timestamp, external_error_code) to be correlated with tenant audit views

Idempotency strategy: prefer idempotency_token checked at adapter + sink (when supported). For sinks without idempotency, use at-least-once with compaction and dedup window. Store short-lived dedup bloom filter keyed by (tenant, compaction_key, hash(payload))
DLQ semantics: unrecoverable events after N retries move to tenant-scoped DLQ with reason codes and a compacted summary; DLQ retention configurable per tenant
Backpressure/flow-control: use adaptive in-flight limits per adapter based on observed sink latency and failure rates; scale adapter workers horizontally for burst absorption
API compatibility: do not change current public audit API; implement relay/adapter internals behind a new feature flag and admin toggle in Console
test_plan: Unit tests for compaction logic covering N=1..10 events with interleaved out-of-order arrivals
Integration test suite that spins up local Splunk emulator and Datadog mock to validate status callbacks and DLQ behavior
Chaos tests: inject transient 500/timeout errors at adapters, verify retry behavior and metrics remain within SLO
Load test: simulate multi-tenant spike with 10k events/sec across 200 tenants and validate compaction window does not exceed memory budgets
Reconciliation test: nightly job compares accepted statuses from sink with Redwood status queue across a 24-hour window and fails if mismatch rate > 0.01% for P1 tenants
rollout_plan: Merge feature behind feature flag to canary environment
Enable for internal tenants + security team for 48 hours and gather telemetry
Enable for 10% of externally-facing tenants (randomized) for 7 days
If metrics stable and no customer regressions, expand to 50% for 7 days, then 100%
Post-rollout: run reconciliation job daily for 14 days and run one postmortem review to capture any lessons
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Compaction increases CPU/memory at relay and may change latency. Mitigation: per-tenant window, memory caps, and fallback to pass-through mode when limits exceeded

Risk: Some external sinks cannot honor idempotency leading to duplicates. Mitigation: emit canonical status events and expose dedup guidance for partners; offer paid connector for sinks that support stronger guarantees
Risk: Increased operational complexity in reconciliation. Mitigation: provide dashboards and automated alerting when sink mismatch rate exceeds threshold
Risk: Security exposure from status callback channel. Mitigation: status channel requires signed tokens and uses tenant-scoped encryption keys; audit logs for all status changes
